chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) permitted regarding Al-Araya that it can be bought by estimating its dates, and said: 'Al-Araya is the plural of Ariyah, and it is the palm tree that belongs to a man in the house of another man, so it is permissible for him to sell it by its estimation of dates, and that is not permissible regarding anything else.'

key_terms.الْعَرَايَا: Plural of Ariyah; palm trees belonging to one person but growing in the land/house of another.
key_terms.تَمْراً: Dates (the fruit of the palm tree), used here as the commodity being estimated and sold.
key_terms.خِرْصِهَا: Estimation or appraisal of the quantity/quality of the produce (dates) before harvest.
key_terms.عَرِيَّة: A loaned item or specifically here, a palm tree situated in another's domain.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling palm trees located in another person's property based on estimated harvest?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates a specific fiqh exception for 'Al-Araya' (p trees in another's land), permitting sale via estimation (khisr) of the expected harvest, a concession distinct from the general prohibition of uncertainty (gharar) in trade. Notably, the Imam clarifies that this flexibility is exclusive to date palms and not applicable to other commodities, reflecting the practical agricultural realities of early Islamic Medina. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on contextualizing prophetic concessions within specific economic and social frameworks.
